Using a ruler and a pair of compasses only, construct a line segment PQ of length 6 cm. Then construct a line through P perpendicular to PQ. Show all construction arcs clearly.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 1 mark for drawing PQ = 6 cm; 1 mark for marking two points A and B on the line either side of P at equal distances from P; 2 marks for arcs from A and B (radius greater than PA) meeting at a point C; 1 mark for joining C to P. The angle between CP and PQ must measure 90°.

items.prompt: Which two instruments are used to construct a perpendicular with arcs rather than with a protractor?
items.answer: A ruler and a pair of compasses

items.prompt: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB of length 7.2 cm. Mark the midpoint of AB as M and label the bisector.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 1 mark for AB = 7.2 cm; 2 marks for arcs of equal radius from A and from B crossing above and below the segment; 1 mark for joining the two crossings; 1 mark for marking M correctly at 3.6 cm from A (and the bisector meeting AB at 90°).

items.prompt: P is a point on the perpendicular bisector of AB and PA = 5 cm. Find PB.
With a ruler and a pair of compasses, construct an angle of 60° and then bisect it. State the size of each of the two parts.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 2 marks for the arcs that give 60° (an equilateral triangle built on a ray); 2 marks for the arc from the vertex that cuts both arms and the final ray from the vertex through the crossing; 1 mark for stating that each part is 30°.

options: They always have the same area

items.answer: They have the same shape but not necessarily the same size

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has vertices A(1, 1), B(4, 1) and C(1, 3). It is translated 3 units to the right to give A'B'C'. Are the triangle and its image congruent? Give a reason.
items.answer: Yes. A translation moves a shape without changing its size or its shape, so the image is congruent to the object.

items.prompt: The sides of one triangle are 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. The sides of another triangle are 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Are the two triangles similar? Give a reason.
items.answer: Yes. Each side of the second triangle is twice the corresponding side of the first, so the sides are in the same ratio and the shapes are the same.

You want to find out how many hours the pupils of your class spend on homework each week. Which method would you use to collect the data, and why?
items.answer: A survey - a questionnaire or an interview - because it asks every pupil the same question and the answers can be recorded as numbers of hours.

items.prompt: Design a questionnaire of four questions to find out how the pupils in your school travel to school. State how you would record the answers.
items.answer: Marking scheme: 1 mark for each sensible question (4 marks); the questions should be closed with answer options such as on foot, bicycle, car, bus, trotro. 1 mark for saying the answers are recorded in a tally chart or frequency table with one row or column for each means of travel.

items.prompt: Write one question you would put in a questionnaire to find out how many people live in each house, together with the answer options you would use.
items.answer: Any closed question, e.g. "How many people live in your house?" with options 1 - 3, 4 - 6, 7 - 9, 10 or more.

options: It lands on heads or on tails

items.prompt: Classify each of these events as impossible, possible or certain: (i) The sun will rise tomorrow. (ii) A fair die shows 7 when it is thrown once.
Give one event from your own life that is impossible and one that is certain.
items.answer: Any sensible pair, e.g. impossible: I will grow wings and fly; certain: I will breathe today.
